source_name: Jobs.cz (LMC) – main Czech professional job board
why_relevant: Dominant CZ white-collar job board; the major banks run their branded microsites on it (kb.jobs.cz, csob.jobs.cz). Role titles such as 'projektový manažer migrace jádrového systému', 'specialista nákupu', 'produktový manažer karty' are the earliest observable indicator of a coming platform/POS replacement programme.

source_name: Prace.cz – second-tier Czech job board
why_relevant: Complementary CZ job board; catches bank supplier/integrator postings (staffing agencies recruiting for bank programmes) that never appear on the bank's own site — an indirect view of which vendor is already staffing a programme.

source_name: Komerční banka career portal (kariera.kb.cz / kb.jobs.cz)
why_relevant: First-party hiring signal from a top-3 CZ bank. KB has a dedicated IT & technology recruitment stream; postings naming a transformation/migration programme, card platform or vendor management reveal buying intent long before any RFP.

source_name: Česká spořitelna career portal (kariera.csas.cz)
why_relevant: Largest CZ retail bank by clients; its own vacancy list is the cleanest first-party signal of internal programmes (payments, cards, merchant acquiring, procurement) that later become tenders or vendor negotiations.

source_name: ČSOB career listings (csob.jobs.cz)
why_relevant: KBC-group bank; hiring for payments/cards/IT-transformation roles indicates group-driven platform programmes with CZ local execution — a lead indicator for local sourcing decisions.

source_name: ČNB – výběrová řízení (Czech National Bank vacancies)
why_relevant: Regulator/operator of CERTIS payment infrastructure. Vacancies in payment-systems, IT infrastructure or procurement units signal ČNB-side infrastructure projects (instant payments, CERTIS modernisation) that pull the whole market.

source_name: LinkedIn – Czech banking/payments job listings and role-change feed
why_relevant: The single richest source for both (a) English-language bank/vendor job ads naming programmes ('core banking migration', 'card platform', 'merchant acquiring') and (b) role changes — a new Head of Payments or Procurement Director is a classic precursor to a re-tender.

source_name: Glassdoor – Prague banking job aggregation
why_relevant: Aggregates English-language bank vacancies in Prague, useful as a cross-check for roles not posted in Czech; also surfaces vendor/consultancy roles staffed against bank programmes.

source_name: Indeed CZ – banking/manager roles
why_relevant: Aggregator that mirrors postings from bank sites and agencies; convenient single query surface for keyword monitoring across many employers.

source_name: Hays Czech Republic – banking & insurance recruitment
why_relevant: Specialist recruiter mandates are often the first externally visible trace of a confidential bank programme (client anonymised as 'a leading bank'). Role titles and skill requirements leak the technology stack being adopted.

source_name: cardforum (SBK) – annual Czech payment-cards conference
why_relevant: The single most on-point event for this cell: organised by Sdružení pro bankovní karty, attended by CZ card issuers, acquirers and terminal vendors. Agendas and speaker lists name the banks and the exact programmes (tokenisation, acceptance modernisation, terminal estate) — a direct read on who is about to buy. Programme is broadcast, and PDF programme files are published per edition.

source_name: Sdružení pro bankovní karty (SBK) / bankovnikarty.cz + cardmag
why_relevant: Trade association of CZ card issuers (~18 members, ~23 observers) — its member/observer list is the authoritative actor map for the card ecosystem, and cardmag is the trade magazine where vendor partnerships and pilots are announced first.

source_name: Retail Summit (Blue Events) – programme and speakers
why_relevant: Largest CEE retail conference (Prague, ~1300 attendees, 80+ speakers). Retailers and their payment/POS partners present roadmaps here; a retailer or bank speaking about checkout/POS renewal is a lead indicator on the merchant side of the acceptance market.

source_name: Blue Events – conference calendar (Prague, cross-sector)
why_relevant: Organiser behind Retail Summit and related CZ/SK B2B conferences; its calendar is a pointer to which industry events exist each year and therefore where bank/retail/payment roadmaps get presented.

source_name: Česká bankovní asociace (ČBA) – kalendář akcí
why_relevant: Banking association event calendar (Finanční konference, transformation conferences). Panel titles and bank speakers reveal sector-level priorities (instant payments, fraud, digital ID) that convert into procurement 6-18 months later.

source_name: Česká fintech asociace – events and working groups
why_relevant: Runs expert working groups and the Fintech Roadmap conference (open banking, digital identity, AI in fintech). Membership list is an actor map of challengers and vendors; event agendas flag pilots before commercial launch.

source_name: Trendy v platebním styku ČR & SR (konferenceseminare.cz)
why_relevant: Dedicated CZ/SK payments conference; 2026 agenda covers tokenisation, PSR/digital euro, payment infrastructure interoperability. Speaker roster is essentially the list of people who own payment-platform budgets in CZ banks.

source_name: ČNB – Národní fórum pro platby (National Forum for Payments)
why_relevant: ČNB-convened multi-stakeholder forum (established 2026) on payment security, fraud prevention and instant payments. Participant lists and meeting outputs are a semi-official early view of mandated changes banks must buy for.

source_name: Zlatá koruna – Czech financial product awards
why_relevant: Longest-running CZ financial product award (since 2003, 24th edition, ~210 products in 24 categories). Award entries force banks to describe new products/platforms publicly and dated — useful for confirming that a platform programme has shipped, and for spotting which vendor stack won.

source_name: Bankovnictví online (bankovnictvionline.cz) – banking trade magazine
why_relevant: CZ banking trade press: carries appointments/role changes, partnership and pilot announcements, and award coverage — the narrative layer that connects a hiring signal to a named programme.

source_name: SystemOnline.cz – IT pro banky a finanční organizace
why_relevant: CZ enterprise-IT magazine with a dedicated banking IT section; publishes vendor-authored case studies naming the bank, the system replaced and the integrator (e.g. payment-system modernisation at MONETA Money Bank) — retrospective confirmation plus a map of who implements for whom.

source_name: MPO – projekt 'Česko platí kartou' (terminal subsidy programme)
why_relevant: State-backed acceptance programme (extended to 31 Mar 2028, 60k+ devices deployed) run with acquirer partners. Partnership announcements and participating-provider lists are a direct, dated signal of terminal-estate volumes and which acquirers are winning merchant share.

source_name: Bank press-release / media centres (e.g. Fio banka tiskové zprávy)
why_relevant: First-party announcements of pricing changes, terminal/gateway offerings, partnerships and pilots. Each major CZ bank runs an equivalent media centre; taken together they are the canonical dated record of pilot and partnership signals.

source_name: MístoProdeje.cz – retail/POS trade portal (interviews, personálie)
why_relevant: Retail/point-of-sale trade portal that publishes interviews with sector figures (e.g. SBK director Roman Kotlán) and vendor/partnership news at the merchant end of the acceptance chain — weak-signal colour that rarely appears in banking press.

source_name: Money Motion (Zagreb) – CEE fintech conference agenda
why_relevant: Largest CEE fintech conference (~150 speakers, 3000+ visitors). Not CZ-hosted, but CZ banks/fintechs speak and announce there; agenda and speaker list are a regional early indicator. Cell brief named it, so scoped in with the caveat that it is Croatia-based.

source_name: Hospodářské noviny – Byznys (HN.cz)
why_relevant: Leading Czech business daily; covers large IT/tech tenders (ministries, banks, state institutions), cancellations, bidder counts and pricing disputes. Confirmed reporting on billion-CZK IT tenders failing for lack of bidders; archive at archiv.hn.cz carries ÚOHS-driven tender rewrites.
